resources.string: Synthetic tests on fixed workloads. They compare this device with itself (before/after a change). A score is not game FPS and does not predict it.
Integer, floating-point and prime-sieve work on one core and on all cores. 1000 points = the fixed single-core workload done in one second. Median of 3 runs.
Copy, read and write bandwidth on 32 MB buffers (MB/s). The score is the copy speed. Median of 3 runs.
Writes and reads a 64 MB file in FrameX\'s own folder (write includes flushing to disk). The read is often served from cache, so it can overstate real read speed. The file is deleted afterwards.
Draws 1500 animated shapes for 8 seconds and measures real frame times in FrameX. It is capped by your display refresh rate and measures FrameX rendering only.
The device is hot (%1$s °C). Cool it down first; hot results are unreliable and heavy load makes it worse.
Tick two results of the same test to compare before and after.
These results come from different devices, so the comparison is not meaningful.
Pick two results of the same test.
